analysis: Documentation-only PR. Changes: (1) docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md adds a head-side paragraph (lines 18-25) separating automatic startup calibration (ModelCalibrationPolicy.startup, EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup) from profile qualification; it states startup calibration only refreshes ordinary rate estimates and does not qualify a timing envelope, raise concurrency or lower memory reserves. The date was bumped to 2026-10-13. (2) docs/developer/test.md (patch, line 1 header onward) adds test descriptions for MiMo FP32 preflight fixtures and startup performance recovery/calibration tests (StartupPerformanceEvidenceTests, ModelCalibrationTests, ProviderLoopCalibrationTests, ProductionModelCalibrationTests). No code, auth, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache storage or billing behavior changes. Cross-file interactions: the new calibration docs describe behavior that lives in unchanged source (ModelCalibrationPolicy, provider loop scheduling), and I did not review that source. The docs claim calibration does not change safety limits (concurrency, memory reserves, deadline envelopes), so a later code PR must preserve that. The test.md patch had a metadata-only unit (:0) with no text. No threat IDs are invalidated and no threat-model update is needed. I found no security regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption. Residual uncertainty is only that the claims about calibration are not verified against code.
